instruction: How do I declare an async function in JavaScript?

instruction: How do I handle rejected promises in JavaScript async/await?
output: Wrap your await call in a `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` block. This structure allows you to catch errors that occur when an await call rejects its promise.

instruction: How do I add an element to the end of an array in JavaScript?
output: Call `.push(element)` on the array instance, such as `arr.push('item')`. This method appends the specified element to the end of the array instance.

instruction: How do I remove the last element of an array in JavaScript?
output: Call `.pop()` on the array instance, such as `const last = arr.pop()`. The method removes and returns that final item from the array instance.

instruction: How do I iterate over an array in JavaScript with element and index?
output: Use `array.forEach((item, index) => { ... })`. This method allows you to access both the current item and its index within each iteration of the array.

instruction: How do I map array elements to a new array in JavaScript?
output: Use `array.map(x => x * 2)` to transform each element. The map function creates a new array by applying the provided callback to each element of the original array.

instruction: How do I filter array elements matching a condition in JavaScript?
output: Use `array.filter(x => x > 10)` to extract matching items. This method extracts items that satisfy the specified condition into a new array.

instruction: How do I check container port mappings in Docker?
output: Run `docker port <container_id>` to view published container ports. This command displays which host ports are mapped to specific container ports for network access.

instruction: How do I restart a running Docker container?
output: Run `docker restart <container_id>` to restart the container. This command restarts the container without changing its name or ID.

instruction: How do I view Docker resource stats in real time?
output: Run `docker stats` to monitor CPU, memory, and network usage per container. This command allows you to monitor CPU, memory, and network usage per container in real time.

instruction: How do I pause execution of a running Docker container?
output: Run `docker pause <container_id>` to suspend container execution. This command suspends container execution without stopping it completely.

instruction: How do I unpause a suspended Docker container?
output: Run `docker unpause <container_id>` to resume execution of a paused container. This command resumes execution of the paused container.

instruction: How do I create a new network in Docker?
output: Run `docker network create my_network` to create an isolated bridge network. This command creates an isolated bridge network named my_network for Docker containers to communicate with each other.

instruction: How do I list all Docker networks?
output: Run `docker network ls` to inspect all configured Docker networks. This command lists all configured Docker networks for inspection.

instruction: How do I create a named Docker volume?
output: Run `docker volume create my_volume` to allocate a persistent storage volume. This command allocates persistent storage for your data.

instruction: How do I list all named Docker volumes?
output: Run `docker volume ls` to list existing persistent Docker volumes. This command lists all named Docker volumes that exist in your current environment.

instruction: How do I select unique values of a column in SQL?
output: Execute `SELECT DISTINCT column_name FROM table_name;` in SQL. This query returns each unique value found in that specific column within the specified table.

instruction: How do I connect to a remote server using SSH on port 2222?
output: Run `ssh -p 2222 user@hostname` to connect via SSH on a custom port. This command connects via SSH on port 2222 to the specified user and hostname.

instruction: How do I copy a local file to a remote server using SCP?
output: Run `scp -P 2222 file.txt user@hostname:/remote/path/`. This command copies the specified local file to the designated remote path on the server using port 2222.

instruction: How do I generate a 4096-bit RSA SSH key pair?
output: Run `ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -C 'email@example.com'`. This command generates an RSA key pair with 4096 bits of length and includes your email address as a comment in the output file.

instruction: How do I copy my public SSH key to a remote server for passwordless login?
output: Run `ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub user@hostname`. This command copies your public key to enable passwordless login for that user and hostname.

instruction: How do I test DNS resolution for a domain name using dig?
output: Run `dig example.com +short` to perform a DNS lookup. This command performs a DNS lookup for example.com and displays the result in short format.

instruction: How do I trace network packet routing hops to a target server?
output: Run `traceroute example.com` or `mtr example.com` to trace network paths. This traces network packet routing hops to a target server.

instruction: How do I check latency and packet loss to a host?
output: Run `ping -c 4 example.com` to send 4 ICMP echo requests. This command sends four ICMP echo requests to check latency and packet loss to the host.

instruction: How do I check systemd service status for nginx?
output: Run `systemctl status nginx` to inspect systemd unit status. This command inspects systemd unit status for nginx.

instruction: How do I restart a systemd service named 'postgresql'?
output: Run `sudo systemctl restart postgresql` to restart the service. This command restarts the postgresql service using systemd's built-in management tools.

instruction: How do I enable a systemd service to start automatically on boot?
output: Run `sudo systemctl enable nginx` to enable auto-start at boot time. This command configures systemd to start nginx automatically when the system boots up.

instruction: How do I view systemd journal logs for unit 'docker'?
output: Run `journalctl -u docker -n 50 --no-pager` to view recent unit logs. This command displays recent logs for the specified unit without using the pager interface.

instruction: How do I check current firewall status in Ubuntu using ufw?
output: Run `sudo ufw status verbose` to view active firewall rules. This command displays active firewall rules in verbose mode to check current status.

instruction: How do I allow incoming port 443 in ufw firewall?
output: Run `sudo ufw allow 443/tcp` to permit incoming HTTPS traffic. This command permits incoming HTTPS traffic on port 443 through ufw.

instruction: How do I generate an MD5 checksum of a file in Linux?
output: Run `md5sum filename` to compute the MD5 hash digest. This command computes the MD5 hash digest for the specified filename.

instruction: How do I generate a SHA256 checksum of a file?
output: Run `sha256sum filename` to compute the SHA256 hash digest. This command computes the SHA256 hash digest for filename as specified in the trusted answer.

instruction: How do I check SSL certificate expiration date for a domain?
output: Run `openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 | openssl x509 -noout -dates`. This command displays the certificate's start and end dates to verify its expiration status.

instruction: How do I create a self-signed SSL certificate using OpenSSL?
output: Run `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 -nodes`. This command generates both the key and certificate files in one step using RSA encryption with 2048-bit strength for three hundred sixty-five days.

instruction: How do I monitor disk I/O activity per process in Linux?
output: Run `sudo iotop` to monitor real-time disk read/write bandwidth by process. This command monitors real-time disk read/write bandwidth by process.

instruction: How do I monitor network throughput per interface in Linux?
output: Run `iftop` or `nload` to monitor real-time network traffic per interface. This allows you to monitor real-time network traffic per interface using iftop or nload.

instruction: How do I find which process is using port 8080?
output: Run `lsof -i :8080` or `fuser 8080/tcp` to identify the owning process. This identifies which process is using port 8080 by listing its owner.

instruction: How do I send a term signal to the process using port 8080?
output: Run `fuser -k -15 8080/tcp` to send a graceful term signal to the process. This command sends a graceful term signal to terminate the process listening on port 8080/tcp.

instruction: How do I check system kernel messages using dmesg?
output: Run `dmesg -T | tail -n 50` to print recent kernel ring buffer messages. This command prints recent kernel ring buffer messages to display them in chronological order with timestamps and limited lines.

instruction: How do I reload Nginx configuration without dropping connections?
output: Run `sudo systemctl reload nginx` or `nginx -s reload`. This reloads Nginx to apply changes without dropping connections.

instruction: How do I test Nginx configuration syntax for errors?
output: Run `sudo nginx -t` to verify configuration syntax before reloading. This command verifies configuration syntax before reloading.

instruction: How do I list active crontab scheduled jobs for current user?
output: Run `crontab -l` to view all configured cron jobs for your user. This command lists all configured cron jobs for your user.

instruction: How do I edit active crontab scheduled jobs?
output: Run `crontab -e` to open the cron schedule configuration in your editor. This command opens your current cron schedule for editing in an editor of your choice.

instruction: How do I schedule a script to run every day at midnight in cron?
output: Add line `0 0 * * * /path/to/script.sh` to your crontab file. This line schedules your script to execute daily at midnight by adding it to your crontab file.

instruction: How do I schedule a script to run every 5 minutes in cron?
output: Add line `*/5 * * * * /path/to/script.sh` to your crontab file. This line tells cron to execute the specified script every five minutes as defined by the schedule pattern.

instruction: How do I set environment variable PATH permanently in Bash?
output: Add `export PATH="/new/path:$PATH"` to your `~/.bashrc` file. This adds the export command to your bashrc so that PATH is updated every time you start a new terminal session.

instruction: How do I reload shell configuration after modifying .bashrc?
output: Run `source ~/.bashrc` to apply the updated environment configuration. This command applies the updated environment configuration to your current session.

instruction: How do I create a zip archive of a directory in Linux?
output: Run `zip -r archive.zip folder_name/` to create a zip file. This command creates a zip archive containing all files and subdirectories within folder_name with an r flag for recursive inclusion.

instruction: How do I unzip a zip file named 'archive.zip'?
output: Run `unzip archive.zip` to extract files from the zip archive. This command extracts files from the zip archive as stated in the original answer.

instruction: How do I download a web page source HTML using wget?
output: Run `wget -O page.html https://example.com` to download page source. This command saves the downloaded HTML content into a file named page.html on your local system.

instruction: How do I sync files from local directory to remote server using rsync?
output: Run `rsync -avz /local/dir/ user@remote:/remote/dir/`. This command copies files from your local directory to the specified remote path on the server.

instruction: How do I perform a dry run of an rsync sync command?
output: Run `rsync -avz --dry-run /local/dir/ user@remote:/remote/dir/`. This command simulates the transfer process without actually moving any files to verify syntax and paths first.

instruction: How do I check open file descriptor limits in Linux?
output: Run `ulimit -n` to view the maximum allowed open file descriptors per process. This command displays the maximum allowed open file descriptors per process.

instruction: How do I temporarily increase open file descriptor limit to 65536?
output: Run `ulimit -n 65536` in your current shell session. This command temporarily increases the open file descriptor limit to 65536 in your current shell session.

instruction: How do I view CPU model and core information in Linux?
output: Run `lscpu` or `cat /proc/cpuinfo` to inspect CPU hardware details. This allows you to view CPU model and core information in Linux as stated in the trusted answer.

instruction: How do I check current system hostname in Linux?
output: Run `hostname` or `hostnamectl` to display the machine hostname. This command displays the machine hostname to identify the current system name for display purposes.

instruction: How do I change machine hostname permanently in Ubuntu?
output: Run `sudo hostnamectl set-hostname new-hostname` to update machine name. This command updates the machine name permanently in Ubuntu.
